options: A category of receipt method
A range of days past due that every open transaction is sorted into based on its due date
A GL account used only for write-offs
A type of customer profile
questions.explain: An aging bucket is a days-past-due range, such as current or 31-60 days, and every open transaction is sorted into exactly one bucket.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a 4-bucket and a 7-bucket aging report?
options: The 7-bucket report only includes paid transactions
The 4-bucket report gives a high-level view, while the 7-bucket report slices the same balances into finer, narrower ranges
The 4-bucket report is only available in a single currency
There is no real difference between them
questions.explain: A 4-bucket report offers broader ranges for a quick overview, while a 7-bucket report provides finer granularity useful for day-to-day collections work.

questions.q: What does an aging report 'by common currency' do?
options: Excludes any customer with multiple currencies
Converts every transaction's balance into a single reporting currency so totals can be compared directly
Only reports balances in US dollars regardless of configuration
Removes currency information from the report entirely
questions.explain: Aging by common currency converts balances into one reporting currency, giving a unified total per bucket for companies invoicing in multiple currencies.

questions.q: What does an aging report 'by collector' allow a collections manager to do?
options: See each collector's assigned portfolio and workload at a glance
Automatically reassign all overdue accounts to a single collector
Bypass approval limits for write-offs
Convert aging data into a customer statement
questions.explain: Aging by collector organizes bucketed aging data by which collector is assigned to each customer, supporting workload visibility for a manager.

questions.q: How does aging data relate to dunning and write-off decisions?
options: It has no connection to either process
It only affects which receipt method a customer uses
It directly drives dunning escalation and provides the evidence trail supporting a write-off decision
It replaces the need for a Collections Workbench
questions.explain: Dunning escalation is often tied to which aging bucket a transaction falls into, and write-off decisions typically rely on aging data showing collections efforts were exhausted.
